text: The majority of concurrent training studies have been carried out with untrained subjects, making it difficult to extrapolate conclusions to physically active people. The few studies that have employed subjects experienced in exercise training indicate greater interference in those who are well trained. Kraemer and colleagues (52) investigated the compatibility of aerobic and resistance exercise in a group of army recruits involved in standard military training for at least 3 days per week for 2 years before the onset of the study. Subjects were randomly assigned to perform aerobic endurance exercise, resistance exercise, or concurrent training.
